what_it_does: Writing a chip blueprint in a hardware description language (like SystemVerilog) is error-prone, and engineers use 'assertions' — checks written into the design that fire an alarm when signals behave unexpectedly — to catch bugs. When an assertion fails, a human engineer must trace through complex timing and logic relationships to find and fix the underlying bug, which is time-consuming and requires deep expertise. AssertSolver is a specialized AI model trained to automate this: given the assertion that failed and the surrounding chip blueprint code, it predicts what the actual bug is and suggests a corrected version of the design. The model was trained on synthetic examples of challenging assertion failures paired with correct fixes, and additionally learned from failure feedback during training to improve its repair accuracy. The paper reports an 88.54% pass rate at producing the correct fix on the first try.
